reviewerNotes: Design is architecturally sound but contains 2 HIGH + 4 MEDIUM findings requiring resolution before implementation. HIGH findings concern operational safety (Debezium snapshot replay risk, field mapping validation). MEDIUM findings address test coverage gaps and clarity issues.

findings.title: Debezium Snapshot Re-Emission Risk — Incomplete Pre-Migration Mitigation
findings.problem: Pre-migration checklist is procedural-only and relies on manual SQL cleanup. If human skips Step 3 or miscalculates grace period, connector will re-emit old events, causing duplicate processing.
findings.concreteFixRequired: Provide automated pre-migration check script that queries for unpublished events >1 hour old and fails deployment if found. Embed in CI/CD pre-flight task. Alternative: Configure Debezium to filter unpublished events during snapshot.
findings.impact: Silent duplicate processing; data consistency issues; idempotency store collisions

findings.title: Debezium Connector Configuration Incomplete — Field Mapping Unvalidated
findings.problem: Design claims field mappings are validated but provides no schema definition. Connector config assumes columns like 'published_at' exist without verification. If schema differs, connector fails silently.
findings.concreteFixRequired: Explicitly document outbox_events table schema in design (DDL provided in review). Add validation step to pre-migration checklist to verify schema matches. Link connector config to schema definition.
findings.impact: Silent connector failure if schema mismatch; events not published to Kafka; SLA violations

findings.title: S6.1 Code Generation Pipeline — buf.gen.yaml pyi Target Misconfiguration
findings.problem: Configuration specifies both 'target: python' and 'target: pyi' writing to same directory with unclear semantics. Typical approach has both outputs side-by-side but not documented.
findings.concreteFixRequired: Clarify buf.gen.yaml with comment explaining pyi + python outputs write to same directory side-by-side. Verify GitHub Actions workflow commits both .py and .pyi files without overwrite.
findings.impact: CI/CD confusion; potential build breakage if outputs collide; unclear output structure

findings.title: S6.3 Idempotency Slow-Path Race Condition — Insert-First Atomicity Assumption
findings.problem: Insert-first pattern relies on catching 'duplicate key' exception, which is fragile. No explicit conflict handling via ON CONFLICT clause. Database session state after exception not documented.
findings.concreteFixRequired: Use PostgreSQL ON CONFLICT clause for truly atomic insert-or-fetch. Provide code example showing two-phase approach (SELECT then INSERT with retry). Document session state guarantees.
findings.impact: Race condition edge case; unlikely but creates technical debt; difficult to debug

findings.title: S6.4 Worker Pool — Async Loop Exit Condition Inefficient
findings.problem: Tight polling loop with fixed 0.1s sleep on empty queue. No backoff escalation. Shutdown race condition if dequeue_message() is slow.
findings.concreteFixRequired: Add exponential backoff (100ms → max 5s) for empty queue sleeps. Alternative: use asyncio.Condition to avoid polling. Document shutdown timeout guarantees.
findings.impact: CPU waste on empty queues; inefficient resource usage; subtle shutdown hangs possible

findings.title: S6.5 Activities — Per-Activity Timeout Not Consistent Across All Activities
findings.problem: Different timeouts specified (60s, 30s, 10s) for each activity without documented justification. Fallback behavior varies (escalate vs graceful degradation) without system. On-call team won't know if timeout is too aggressive.
findings.concreteFixRequired: Add table documenting timeout rationale for each activity (LLM inference needs 60s buffer, pure logic needs 10s, etc.). Explain fallback strategy per activity. Link workflow definition to activity timeouts.
findings.impact: Operational confusion; risk of overly aggressive timeouts causing unnecessary escalations

findings.title: S6.6 Feature Flags — Mutual Exclusion Enforcement Not Testable
findings.problem: Design claims mutual exclusion enforcement but only exists in application code. No test explicitly verifies 'if MVP, then NOT Kafka'. Both adapters running concurrently with no infrastructure-level enforcement.
findings.concreteFixRequired: Add integration test that verifies message goes to exactly ONE adapter. Add metrics (event_published_kafka, event_published_mvp) to alert if mutual exclusion violated.
findings.impact: Subtle bug potential; duplicate processing if adapter selection logic breaks; hard to detect

findings.title: S6.6 Parity Checker — Threshold Justification Missing
findings.problem: Threshold constants (2% intent divergence, 5% confidence difference, 10% entity count) specified without justification. On-call team won't know if 1.5% divergence is OK or a problem.
findings.concreteFixRequired: Add design rationale section explaining: why 2% intent (model equivalence), why 5% confidence (autonomy decision threshold), why 10% entities (deterministic extractor). Explain action for each threshold breach.
findings.impact: Operational clarity gap; poor on-call decision-making; risk of false alerts or missed issues
